Lead and Copper Rule.name: Lead and Copper Rule
Lead and Copper Rule.plain: The rule governing lead and copper monitoring and corrosion control. A violation is often procedural — a missed sampling round or a late report.

Lead.plain: Lead is almost never in water at its source. It gets picked up on the way to the tap — from the service line under the street, from solder in older joints, from the brass in the tap itself. That makes it a property of your building more than of your town.
Lead.effect: Infants and children who drink water containing lead in excess of the action level could experience delays in their physical or mental development. Children could show slight deficits in attention span and learning abilities. Adults who drink this water over many years could develop kidney problems or high blood pressure.
Lead.source: U.S. EPA, mandatory health effects language — Lead and Copper Rule

Combined Radium (-226 and -228).plain: Radium is naturally radioactive and dissolves out of certain rock formations into groundwater. Like arsenic, it is a feature of local geology.
Combined Radium (-226 and -228).effect: Some people who drink water containing radium 226 or 228 in excess of the maximum contaminant level over many years may have an increased risk of getting cancer.
Combined Radium (-226 and -228).source: U.S. EPA, mandatory health effects language — Radionuclides
